A basis is just our coordinate grid.
Vectors are arrows, independent of grids.
Different grids give different coordinate descriptions.

Show vector v=(x,y) as linear combination of i-hat and j-hat.
Highlight scalar coefficients x and y.

Lecture lines:
Same vector, different perspectives.
We need a bridge between systems.
Changing coordinates preserves the physical vector.

Planned animations:
Display object in standard basis grid #FFFFFF.
Rotate coordinate system grid, keeping object fixed.
Show the challenge of describing constant position in new coordinates.

Lecture lines:
Define the transition matrix P.
Columns are new basis in old.
Equation: vector B equals P, vector C.
P maps coordinates between bases.
The bridge is built.

Planned animations:

Draw arrow from old basis to matrix structure.

Lecture lines:
Identify new and old basis vectors.
Construct the transition matrix P.
Multiply P by new coordinates.
Result is old coordinate vector.

Highlight matrix elements, then vector elements.
Display resulting coordinates v_new step-by-step.

Friendly bases make math easier.
Example: switching to camera space.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application & Summary", [
            "Simplifying transformations is our goal.",

        self.play(Rotate(wireframe, angle=PI/4, about_point=wireframe.get_center()))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)

        self.place_in_area(render_result, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(render_result), FadeOut(wireframe))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)
